key_insight: GEAR shows that image tokenizers and autoregressive generators work better when trained together instead of separately. By guiding the tokenizer with the generator’s needs, the model learns representations that are easier to generate and can improve synthesis quality.
problem_solved: Traditional visual generative pipelines train a tokenizer first and freeze it before training the generator. This decoupling can produce latent codes that reconstruct images well but are not optimal for autoregressive generation.
method: Jointly trains a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer and an autoregressive (AR) generator end-to-end.
Uses representation alignment to guide the tokenizer toward latents that are both reconstructive and easy for the generator to model.
Optimizes the two components together so the learned discrete image representation better matches generation dynamics.
impact: This matters because it closes the gap between compression/reconstruction and generation quality. For practitioners, it suggests a more effective training strategy for visual generative models that can improve sample quality and model efficiency.

paper_title: GEAR: Guided End-to-End AutoRegression for Image Synthesis
paper_authors: Bin Lin, Zheyuan Liu, Chenguo Lin, Sixiang Chen, Yunyang Ge
